answer: Each identity files one karst-cut crystal at the wharf registry and locks 70 credits. Its seal binds key, bench and epoch; auditors replay each crystal on the karst log, and reuse, copying or wrong bench burns the bond. First filing costs 40, then 40+6(k-1): 1,000 fakes pay 3,037,000 and lock 70,000 for a 40,000 pool. A rented seal carries its owner's key, so a second wharf filing burns both bonds. Honest agents file once, pay 40, keep a share.
